Space Marine 2 is a mixed bag. On one hand, the singleplayer campaign is an excellently made third-person shooter that does little to push any boundaries. It's a pure visual treat and 40k fans will be pleasantly surprised with lots of fan service and cool moments. As a friend of mine said, it's basically Catholic Gears of War. That's not quite accurate, but it's about 80% of the way there. Throw in a little God of War and Doom and you basically have Space Marine 2. It's a solid amalgam of popular shooter tropes that's roughly 6-8 hours long and the difficulty felt well-balanced on the recommended hard mode.

However, the problem with the game comes with the multiplayer. If you have 2 other friends to play coop with, you can ignore this section since it mostly covers matchmaking, the missions themselves are a fun way to extend the story for a few hours despite being much lighter on story content than the main campaign. The matchmaking is horrendous and ruins the multiplayer experience entirely. While the issues are almost too numerous to list, I will attempt to list the main ones.

Firstly, there is no way to choose to play a mission from the start if you've never played it before, selecting that mission is likely to put you into a match that has already started. If you are put into a match that has already started, you may not be able to play the class that you want since there's no way to know if it's already been selected by a player in that match. There's no way to choose to host a match and whoever the lucky winner is can kick whoever they want from a game, even near the very end to deprive others of progress.

Furthermore, the Quick Match functionality is broken and is more likely to put you into the hub area of some AFK player than actually put you into a match. You will also spend at least half of your time trying to play multiplayer looking for a match and staring at an empty black loading screen of which the game has many and are so numerous you would think you're playing Morrowind on the OG Xbox, and this is with a modern SSD.

I would not recommend the game if you plan on playing multiplayer without a dedicated group of friends because the price of the singleplayer alone is not worth it in my opinion.

Single player and ops are pretty cool, but you run out of content fast. Me and my friend had it all beat in about one sitting. I payed 30$ when it was on sale which feels steep given how little content their is. The eternal war sucks ass. No match making balance I never played one match that was remotely close its either stomp or get stomped. That is to say your team is either so much better then the enemy theirs no chance you could lose or so bad theirs no chance you can win. And ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ unending stun grenades for days. Gave up on eternal war after 3 days of forcing myself to try it. Honestly if you can pick the game up for 20 its worth it for the campaigns and the ops, but at 60$ pass pass pass.

The game looks, sounds, and plays great. Would recommend installing on an SSD if possible as I had some audio separation issues in cutscenes and after swapping it over those were resolved. My only qualm is that the story feels a bit short, but you can definitely tell how much effort and care was put into this game. The level of customization in multiplayer is also great (at least for the imperium side), being able to rep the salamanders in PVP and PVE is great. All in all I'd say this game is a 8/10, I wouldn't pay full price for it but getting it on sale is definitely worthwhile.

I have no words to describe what I'm feeling now that I've just finished this game. It wasn't perfect, at times it was even boring, but the highlights of this game more than make up for it. Way more. It's a faith-restoring game. Do not stop before you finish the campaign, you'll be losing the experience of a generation. 

Easily the best game I've played since Doom eternal. And it made me a HUGE fan of warhammer. What a fantastic lore, world. I need this series to keep going.
